alignments.note: The waw is rendered Then, which the ASV's open connective list includes (rule 14).
Finite verb with its subject pronoun, headed on said (rules 17, 24).
Sit still renders the verb with its phrasal particle; the bare Sit does not write the remaining, so the particle completes the lexeme and the head stays on the verb (rule 44).
Vocative noun; its possessive is the suffix's (rule 36).
Suffix takes my (rule 18).

The preposition and the relative are rendered by the single until, which carries both the temporal limit and the subordination, so rule 30's one-English-word condition is met and the pair shares a unit; no morpheme is left unrepresented beside a word carrying its sense (rules 30, 22). No morpheme carries content the other lacks, so the head is the governing morpheme standing first (rule 23), exactly as ki im is read later in this verse.
Finite verb with its subject pronoun, headed on know.
Paragogic nun has no English realization (rule 32).
Interrogative rendered how.
Finite verb with its auxiliary, headed on fall.
No article morpheme stands here, so the supplied the belongs to the nominal expression it determines (rule 15).
The particle takes the for written for it (rule 14).
Negative takes not.
Finite verb with its auxiliary, headed on rest; the unit is discontinuous around the negative (rule 25).
Article takes the.
Noun rendered man.
The compound particle is rendered by the single until; rule 30's one-word condition is met and the pair shares a unit headed on the governing morpheme (rule 23).
Finite verb with subject pronoun and auxiliary, headed on finished.
Article takes the.
Noun rendered thing.
The demonstrative this stands where the phrase's the would stand and is what the ASV writes for the article, no demonstrative pronoun standing in the phrase (rule 41).
Noun rendered day.

review_notes: Corrected: ad asher is now one fused unit on the single until, headed on the preposition, rather than the preposition taking the word with the relative unrepresented. The one English word carries the temporal limit and the subordination alike, so rule 30's condition is met and rule 22's first sentence, which governs an element the ASV has left unwritten, does not reach it; rule 30 forbids leaving a morpheme whose sense the rendering carries unrepresented. This also makes the verse consistent with the ki im fusion later in the same clause chain.
Head on the opening morpheme in both fusions, since neither pair has a morpheme carrying content the other lacks and the syntactic head is the one standing first (rule 23).
The matter takes a supplied the, no article morpheme standing on that noun (rule 15).
